title: Select pilot customers for air-gapped signed offline bundles + define success criteria and comms plan
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
project: Redwood Private – On-prem offline artifact signing
description:
Context
We need 2–3 pilot customers with real air-gapped constraints to validate the end-to-end workflow for signed offline bundles (build → transport → verify → install/upgrade → audit evidence). This ticket selects pilot accounts, defines success criteria per customer, and sets timelines/comms/enablement so Support/SE aren’t improvising.

Pilot goals (what we must learn)
- Do customers successfully verify signatures in a truly offline environment (no outbound network; restricted tooling)?
- Are failures actionable (clear error codes, log paths, remediation steps) and do we fail closed by default?
- Can customers operationalize key/trust store updates and upgrades without Redwood hands-on each time?
- Are audit artifacts sufficient for security teams (local logs, support bundle output, evidence mapping)?

Proposed pilot cohort
Pilot A (Defense / strict air-gap): Helios Defense
- Why: Highest supply-chain sensitivity; strict media handling; strongest signal on verification UX and failure modes.
- Constraints: Air-gapped enclave, limited time sync, hardened hosts, strict change-control.
- Primary contacts: Security + platform ops (via SE/CS).

Pilot B (Regulated finance): AsterBank
- Why: Strong audit requirements, will pressure test documentation/evidence and key rotation readiness.
- Constraints: Formal security review gates; requires SIEM/export path clarity.
- Primary contacts: Security architecture + infra.

Pilot C (Healthcare / offline POC): Northbridge Health (optional / stretch if capacity)
- Why: Different ops maturity and install environment; good for validating docs clarity and minimum viable workflow.
- Constraints: Partial offline (limited egress), smaller team, wants “recipe” style guide.

Not selected for initial pilot (keep warm)
- GovLab Research: Good fit but procurement/legal gating likely to slow feedback loop; revisit for GA readiness validation.
- Ion Fabrication: Interesting operational constraints (factory floor) but timing uncertain; candidate for post-GA hardening.

Pilot success criteria (global, applies to all)
1) Verification works offline
- Customer can run preflight verification against a provided bundle and get a deterministic PASS/FAIL.
- Installer blocks install on signature mismatch, unknown key, or manifest hash mismatch (no silent fallback).

2) Transport integrity is detectable
- If bundle is corrupted during transfer/unzip, verification fails with a clear “hash mismatch” classification and remediation guidance.

3) Upgrade path validated
- Customer installs from signed bundle N and successfully upgrades to signed bundle N+1.
- Downgrade attempt is blocked (or requires explicit break-glass if policy allows) and is auditable.

4) Key/trust store story is operational
- Customer can update trust store in an air-gapped way using documented steps.
- Key rotation scenario is explained and at least table-top exercised during pilot (AsterBank required; Helios recommended).

5) Audit artifacts produced locally
- Verification outcome is written to local logs/audit events; support bundle includes manifest + signature status.
- Redaction defaults are acceptable; no secrets or payloads inadvertently logged.

6) Support readiness
- Support/SE can resolve at least one induced failure scenario using runbooks only (no engineer required), e.g. corrupted transfer, unknown key, time skew.

Customer-specific success criteria / scope
Helios Defense (Pilot A)
- Must validate time skew / no-NTP guidance: demonstrate verification success with documented time source assumptions.
- Must validate “never fetch” behavior: installer must not attempt any downloads in air-gapped mode.
- Must validate break-glass policy path exists but is not required for normal install.

AsterBank (Pilot B)
- Must validate audit evidence package: provide list of artifacts (bundle manifest, signature envelope, installer verification logs) and where they live.
- Must validate key rotation readiness: customer can install trust store update and verify a bundle signed by the new key.
- Must validate downgrade protection messaging for auditors (what is blocked, what is logged).

Northbridge Health (Pilot C, optional)
- Must validate “minimum operator steps”: can complete install following doc with minimal tribal knowledge.
- Must validate troubleshooting flow for common errors (hash mismatch after transfer, unknown key, not-yet-valid).

Pilot timeline (target)
- 2025-12-09 to 2025-12-13: confirm customer availability + internal owners + NDA/data handling notes.
- 2025-12-16: pilot kickoff packet to each customer (what’s new, required installer version, checklist).
- 2026-01-06: deliver RC signed bundle + installer build to Helios + AsterBank.
- 2026-01-07 to 2026-01-17: installations + verification + induced failure exercises.
- 2026-01-20: upgrade test (N → N+1) + key rotation table-top (AsterBank).
- 2026-01-22: pilot exit review + punchlist for GA gating (docs/runbooks/product gaps).

Comms + cadence
- Dedicated Slack channels per pilot (internal): #pilot-helios-airgap, #pilot-asterbank-airgap, #pilot-northbridge-offline (if enabled).
- Weekly 30-min customer check-in + async daily status for the first install week.
- Single “pilot coordinator” per account:
  - Helios: Fatima Noor (SE) + Rachel Kim (CS)
  - AsterBank: Colin O’Donnell (SE) + Rachel Kim (CS)
  - Northbridge: Bruno Silva (PS) + Rachel Kim (CS)
- Escalation path: Support (Dev Patel) → Eng on-call (Sean Gallagher) → Installer eng lead (Ethan Park) → Release eng (Connor O’Brien) depending on symptom.

Deliverables to provide to each pilot customer
- Signed offline bundle + detached signature files + checksum guidance.
- Required installer version + verification commands (preflight + inspect).
- One-page “What to do if verification fails” with log locations and error code meanings.
- Key/trust store update instructions (air-gapped).
- Evidence list for security review (AsterBank required).

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Customer environment cannot provide reliable time source → signature validity issues.
  - Mitigation: Document acceptable time sources; provide diagnostic-only override guidance; prefer signatures that don’t require online checks.
- Risk: Media transfer tooling corrupts bundle (zip/unzip, line endings, AV scanning).
  - Mitigation: Provide explicit packaging recommendations; ensure hash mismatch messaging is crisp; add “inspect bundle” pre-check step.
- Risk: Over-rotating keys during pilot causes confusion.
  - Mitigation: Freeze signing key during initial install week; perform rotation exercise only after baseline success.

Exit criteria
- Helios + AsterBank both complete install + verify + upgrade without break-glass.
- At least 1 induced failure is successfully diagnosed by Support/SE using runbook.
- GA punchlist is captured and owners assigned (docs + engineering).

Open questions
- Do we require pilots to test SIEM export now or accept “local logs only” for pilot and validate export post-pilot?
- What’s the minimum “evidence packet” AsterBank needs to unblock procurement vs. what we include at GA?

Owners

- Partners: Fatima Noor, Colin O’Donnell, Bruno Silva, Dev Patel, Connor O’Brien, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov

2025-12-06 (Marcus Lin): Security ask: pilots must include at least one key rotation scenario (can be table-top if we can’t safely rotate during the window). Also ensure we validate “unknown key” behavior fails closed with explicit error classification.

2025-12-09 (Rachel Kim): Helios confirmed they can schedule an install window week of Jan 6; requires advance checklist and named escalation contacts. AsterBank wants evidence list up front for security sign-off; asked for where verification events are logged and retention guidance.

2025-12-12 (Olga Petrov): For AsterBank, include mapping to common controls language (integrity/provenance, change control, audit logging). Daniel Carter can help assemble a lightweight evidence packet for the pilot.

2026-01-05 (Fatima Noor): Helios will only accept transfer via encrypted removable media; they asked us to state preferred archive format and exact hash verification command(s). Requested we standardize on one ‘inspect’ command output for screenshots.

2026-01-10 (Dev Patel): Support request: for the induced failure exercise, please pick a ‘hash mismatch after transfer’ scenario and an ‘unknown signing key’ scenario so we can validate runbook coverage before GA.

2026-01-22 (Rachel Kim): Marked done — cohort confirmed (Helios + AsterBank; Northbridge on standby). Kickoff packets sent; schedule and success criteria aligned with Security/Support. Remaining work tracked in pilot execution checklist under PM-894.
